name: month
description: Reference month of the observation, from 1 to 12
observations: Derived from the BLS period code M01-M12; NULL on annual-average rows, which carry period_id M13

name: period_id
description: BLS period code identifying the month or the annual average
observations: BLS period code as published. M01-M12 are months; M13 is the annual average BLS publishes in the same files, on which month is NULL

name: series_id
observations: Kept alongside the decomposed dimensions so a series can be looked up directly against BLS. Example: CES0000000001, all employees on total nonfarm payrolls, seasonally adjusted

name: supersector_id
description: CES supersector the industry belongs to

name: industry_id
observations: An 8-digit BLS code whose first two digits repeat the supersector and whose remaining six are a right-zero-padded NAICS code. It is a BLS hierarchy rather than NAICS itself, so no directory link is declared on it; naics_id carries the resolvable NAICS code

name: naics_id
description: NAICS code the CES industry corresponds to
observations: Taken from the naics_code field of ce.industry, and NULL where no single code applies: CES aggregates carry either no NAICS equivalent, a list of sibling codes, or a part-of-industry marker. Codes are published against the NAICS vintage current at release; the link is declared against NAICS 2022

name: data_type_id
description: CES data type, which fixes what the value measures
observations: Employment counts, average weekly hours, average hourly and weekly earnings, aggregate hours and payrolls, diffusion indexes, and collection response rates all share the value column

name: seasonal_adjustment
description: Whether the series is seasonally adjusted (S) or not seasonally adjusted (U)
observations: A dimension of the series, not a footnote: adjusted and unadjusted values for the same cell are different numbers and must never be mixed

name: value
description: Published value of the series for the period
observations: Units differ by row and are given in measurement_unit, so no single column-level unit applies. BLS prints - for an observation that was not published; those are NULL, not zero

name: measurement_unit
description: Unit the value is measured in
observations: Derived by Data Basis from the dimension that fixes the unit (data type for CES, measure for LAUS, rate-or-level for JOLTS); not published as a field by BLS

name: footnote_id
description: BLS footnote code attached to the observation
observations: NULL when the observation carries no footnote. Codes flag preliminary and revised values and, in 2025, observations missing because of the lapse in appropriations
